role: evidence for the E11 H4 (transverse box-limit correction) bracket; not a confirmatory result and not an error bar on the limit
question: At w = 3.2 mm, does the transverse box-limit correction move Z0 by >= 0.10 ohm (>= 0.2 percent, >= 0.13 pp of the residual) as frozen in docs/design/E11_residual_preregistration.md section 2, Bracket H4 (lines 145-148)?

input_ladder.git_rev_recorded_in_ladder: unavailable (git not installed in workspace container)
input_ladder.box_rule: the lateral Neumann walls sit n_clean cells each side of the strip, the top wall n_air cells above it; the thin direction is one periodic cell

not_an_error_bar.covariance_note: the covariance curve_fit returns on a 4-point 3-parameter fit is an over-fitting number, not an uncertainty; it is recorded for completeness and MUST NOT be quoted as an error bar on the limit
not_an_error_bar.why: the 4-point 3-parameter curve_fit covariance is an over-fitting artefact; the uncertainty reported here is the spread of independent estimators, not the covariance

estimator_spread.interpretation: the span of the five cross-check estimators computed from the same four rungs (the 4-point refit itself, 48.02374054929774, lies inside the interval) is the only defensible uncertainty on the limit that this ladder supports. It is not a rigorous error bar and it is not the covariance.

box_limit_correction.why_zero: the ladder measures Z0(n) with the transverse box widened at every rung so that the box is a fixed multiple of the structure, and z0_inf_ohm is the n -> infinity limit of THAT sequence: 48.02374054929774 already IS the wide-box limit. There is no second box-limit correction left to apply, so the correction is identically zero by construction, not by measurement.

threshold.derivation: 0.10 / 48.02374054929774 = 0.2082 percent; times |dlnGamma/dlnZ0| = 0.657646 = 0.1369 pp of the residual

comparison_to_threshold.verdict_basis: the only live quantity is the 0.024136399 ohm estimator span, which is 24 percent of the 0.10 ohm threshold; the crisp box-limit correction is zero

worth_in_residual_currency.reading: the whole box-limit question is worth 0.0331 pp out of a 4.904 pp residual, i.e. 0.67 percent of the discrepancy. It cannot explain the residual and it cannot rescue it.

alternative_reading_if_n200_is_the_limit.why_this_reading_is_not_taken: if the finest rung were taken as the limit instead of the n -> infinity fit, the "box-limit correction" would become the n=200 truncation gap, which is an extrapolation error and not a box-limit effect at all. Even then it is worth only 0.2538 pp = 5.2 percent of the residual, so H4 would fire as "real but small" and still not matter. Recorded so the paperwork cannot be accused of taking only the weak reading.

dr36_is_w3.0mm_not_w3.2mm.claim: DR-36 reports a 0.91 percent drift and a 0.37 percent extrapolation gap.
dr36_is_w3.0mm_not_w3.2mm.resolution: DR-36 is the w = 3.0 mm ladder (docs/design/EM_SOLVER_LEDGER.md:623). Neither figure is a w = 3.2 mm measurement and neither transfers to this bracket.

two_quantities_under_one_label.resolution: the bracket text runs the box-limit correction and the estimator uncertainty together under a single "correction" label. They are different quantities: a modelling offset and a convergence error. H4 as written cannot distinguish them, which is why this artefact reports both, separately.

category_error_at_line_143.resolution: the bracket presumes a box-limited value exists that differs from 48.02374054929774 and is waiting to be corrected. It does not: 48.02374054929774 is already the wide-box limit of this ladder. Asking for its box-limit correction is a category error, so the correction is 0 and the only live number is the 0.024136399 ohm estimator span.
